Quality_final_shape_description:
The gear is formed by first creating a central cylindrical web section with an outer diameter of 3.500 inches and an axial length of 0.775 inches. On the outer circumference of the central 0.625 inch portion of this web, 32 gear teeth are cut, resulting in an overall outside diameter of 4.000 inches, a pitch diameter of 3.500 inches, and a root diameter of 2.000 inches. The tooth profile is further defined by radii R2.125 (to the tooth tip) and R2.375 (to the tooth root), and by vertical coordinates 1.875, 3.75, 7.5, and 9.375 (units unclear) from the gear's centerline. 

Attached to each axial end of this central web section is a tapered web section. Each tapered web is a frustum of a cone, transitioning from a larger diameter of 3.500 inches (at the central web) to a smaller diameter of 2.000 inches, with an axial length of 0.475 inches. 

Finally, a cylindrical hub is attached to the smaller diameter end of each tapered web. Each hub has an outer diameter of 2.000 inches and an axial length of 0.450 inches. The total overall axial length of the gear is 2.625 inches. 

A central through-bore of 1.500 inches diameter runs axially through the entire gear. A keyway, 0.192 inches wide and 0.096 inches deep (from the bore surface), is cut into the bore for an axial length of 0.812 inches, centered axially. Four internal fillets with a radius of 0.125 inches are present at the junctions where the tapered webs meet the hubs and where the tapered webs meet the central web section.
